title: Regular codimension-two boundary away from an integral divisor generic point
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and $i:D\to L$ an effective Cartier centre [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], with $D$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $U\subseteq L$ be open with $z\in U$ exactly when $z$ is outside the image of $i$. Let $W\subseteq L$ be open containing $i(\eta_D)$, where $\eta_D$ is the unique generic point of the integral scheme $D$. Then for every $z\notin U\cup W$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{L,z}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and has Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] at least two.

source.place: Tags 0EYE, proof (regularity on the divisor); 00NU (algebra-lemma-regular-local-quotient-by-regular-sequence); 0EYJ, trait paragraph; dimension calculation for a Cartier nonzerodivisor

proof.text: Write z=i(d), using the complement condition. Since the image of the generic point belongs to W, d is not the generic point. The local defining ideal of the effective Cartier centre is generated by a nonzerodivisor f in the maximal ideal and the quotient stalk is the regular local ring of D at d. By 00NU the ambient Noetherian stalk is regular.

In an integral scheme the stalk at a nongeneric point has dimension at least one: on an affine neighbourhood its corresponding nonzero prime contains the zero prime properly. Quotienting a Noetherian local ring by a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal lowers dimension by one. Thus the ambient stalk has dimension at least two. This is precisely the remaining closed boundary after adjoining W.
